newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Short stg volatility holds at low levels.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Short stg volatility holds at low levels.

text.p: Implied volatility of options on short sterling futures remained steady at low levels on Thursday as prospects of a British interest rate rise before the election receded, brokers said.
Earlier the British Chamber of Commerce said it did not expect to see a rate rise before the election, but would expect an increase shortly after the election. A British election must be held by May.
"Short sterling vols have fallen over the last few days," said an options broker on the LIFFE floor. "After the survey this morning there doesn't seem to be much hope of a rate hike."

Brokers quoted implied volatility of options on short sterling futures at around 7.0 percent for March, 10 percent for June, 12.5 percent for September, and 14.65 percent for December, all more or less unchanged from yesterday.
"Volatility has slipped a long way and is very low, whether it can come much lower is open to debate," the broker said.
He said the ruling Conservative party was likely to make every effort to keep rates as low as possible in the run up to the election.

"They won't want to put rates up if they can help it and they certainly have a few more excuses up their sleeves than they did in December. It's on that basis that short sterling vols have come off recently," he said.
Brokers said the market had been quite active during the session.

"People have been taking advantatge of volatility at these levels," said a broker at a British brokerage in London. "We have seen paper buyers of volatility but conversely we have seen some paper sellers. Mainly it is still directional trading by paper."
Paper refers to institutions which trade for clients as opposed to locals who trade for their own account.
The broker on the LIFFE floor said there had been a lot of call buying of the June, September, December strips and that was shoring up volatility levels.
